firstPlayerRule: Randomly choose which player goes first. The starting player begins with 2 magic, and the opponent begins with 3 magic.
clarifications: Set up each player's starting cards and draw five cards before choosing the starting player and assigning starting magic.
Players alternate complete turns. After completing the five phases of a turn, draw back up to five cards before the opponent takes a turn.
The setup instruction covers both faction decks and custom decks in this rulebook.

internalEvidence: Reopened Plaid Hat Games' official Summoner Wars page and followed its rulebook link. Its current label says v2, but the linked file is ph3600-rulebook-v1_2.pdf and its cover identifies v1.2; this record is scoped to that file. A live download matched cached SHA-256 560161fb72f4c36f3dc6e23259061ab51ce480bd6acc4dbf19575ff96cb8bb50. Inspected complete rendered PDF pages 1, 5, 6 and 20, plus searched the full extracted manual for starting and turn-order context. Setup step 6 randomly selects the starter and gives that player 2 magic versus the opponent's 3; preceding steps cover deck choice, starting cards and five-card hands. Page 6 specifies alternating complete turns and refilling to five. Page 20 has a 2021 copyright, which is not treated as a v1.2 release date. Editorial review 2026-09-26: The linked PDF itself identifies v1.2 despite the current publisher link label. Setup selects randomly after hands and assigns 2 versus 3 magic; complete turns alternate. No newest-version claim or first-edition transfer. Random choice and component compensation exclude portable enrollment. Codex independently inspected the cited source context and all public fields. Owner authorization: factual review delegated to Codex on 2026-09-22. This exact reviewed revision is approved for the catalog; earlier draft-only statements describe intake history. No deployment approval.
uncertainty: The reviewed manual does not prescribe the random selection method or a separate starting-player tie procedure.
The publisher's link label and the PDF version differ. This answer makes no claim about the newest rulebook or other editions.
